subject: Request: DPA amendment — no-model-learning + prompt/response ownership (SanaHealth)
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena.petrova@sanahealth.eu>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sana-legal@sanahealth.eu
Date: 2026-11-15T08:12:00Z
Subject: DPA amendment request — operational evidence and prompt ownership

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal has reviewed the standard DPA and pushed back on a couple of items we need to close before procurement can sign:

1) A firm no-model-learning / no adaptive training commitment for our tenant data (we need language that covers both bulk ingestion and interactive sessions).
2) Explicit assignment of prompt-and-response ownership to SanaHealth (clarify that generated responses based on customer prompts are treated as customer outputs).
3) List of subprocessors and the cross-border transfer mechanism for backups/analytics — we prefer SCCs plus onshore routing for EU tenants where possible.
4) Operational evidence that KV cache/prefix caching will not result in persistent model updates and details on retention/TTL for transient data.

I've attached a redline (SanaHealth_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and our subprocessor matrix. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide:
- A short operational attestation (PDF) describing KV cache TTL, batching behavior, and whether any telemetry is retained beyond 30 days;
- A DocuSign-able DPA amendment we can send to procurement;
- A timeline for when engineering can provide a short technical note for our security team?

We need to close this by EOD Tuesday to keep our migration window.

Best,
Elena Petrova
Head of Security & Privacy, SanaHealth

Subject: Proposed DPA amendment language (no-model-learning + outputs ownership)

Elena / Marissa —

Thanks — attaching a proposed amendment text (I pasted the key clauses below). High level: we will commit contractually to no-model-learning for customer tenant data ("no adaptive training or model updates using Customer Data") and to clarify that customer prompts and the corresponding generated responses are Customer Outputs, subject to the customer's IP rights. We also add an attestation requirement and operational proof delivery timeline.

Proposed clauses (summary):
- No-Model-Learning: Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or update models that would result in persistent model improvements outside of explicit, documented opt-in processes agreed in writing. This applies to all customer-originated prompts, uploads, and interaction logs.
- Outputs Ownership: Customer retains ownership of Prompt Content and Generated Outputs. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, royalty-free license to any derivative service artifacts solely to the extent necessary for service delivery.
- Subprocessor & Transfers: Redwood will maintain a current Subprocessor list and will (i) apply SCCs for transfers from the EU to non-EEA processors, and (ii) provide options for onshore routing where operationally feasible.
- Operational Attestation: Redwood will provide an ops attestation describing KV cache ephemeral TTLs, non-retention of content beyond N days (we propose 30 days), and telemetry minimization.

I have redlined your DPA (see SanaHealth_DPA_redline_v3.docx) with these clauses and marked items that require procurement review (e.g., strict export restrictions or indefinite retention requests).

Once you OK the language, I will:
1) convert to an amendment (DocuSign-ready PDF),
2) add standard signature blocks, and
3) include the subprocessor annex.

Note: two procurement asks may require internal signoff — (a) if you require onshore-only processing for all backups we need to confirm availability in the target regions and (b) if you require shorter TTLs than 30 days we will run an ops feasibility check.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Ops attestation draft + technical notes (KV caching, retention, telemetry)

Hi Elena — per Marissa/Kimberly, here's the ops note we can attach to the DPA amendment. Attaching a formal PDF (ops_evidence_kv_ttl.pdf). Key points summarized below.

Operational attestation (summary):
- KV / Prefix Caching: Redwood uses ephemeral KV caches for active sessions. Cache entries are stored in memory on serving nodes and are not persisted to long-term training datasets.
- TTLs: Default TTL for ephemeral caches is 6 hours; for queued request traces (used for debugging) retention is 30 days by default and can be shortened by agreement to 14 or 7 days for EU tenants based on an SLA amendment.
- No persistent training: There is no background job that automatically incorporates tenant data into model training. Any dataset used for research or improvement requires a documented opt-in workflow and explicit dataset extraction, with customer-level identifiers removed unless customer consent is provided.
- Telemetry: Aggregate telemetry (latency, error rates) is retained for 12 months for platform reliability; request-level payload telemetry is minimized and scrubbed. We can enable limited onshore-only logging for EU customers under a Dedicated or Private deployment.

Operational limitations / asks:
- Onshore-only backups for all EU data require Dedicated region capacity or Private deployment — otherwise SCCs will be used for transfers.
- Shorter retention (under 30 days) for traces is possible but may limit debugging efficiency; we'll document the support process in the amendment.

Timeline:
- Ops attestation PDF (attached): ready now.
- Implementation feasibility check for 14-day trace TTL and onshore-only backups: 3 business days.

If this meets your needs I can convert the attached PDF into the evidence annex Kimberly references.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
